plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable or USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages exclusion preserving data-restoration and replacement costs as direct, and Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check mutuality and that the cap is not undercut elsewhere (e.g., insurance non-limitation in 18.2).

No indemnification section appears in the outline (numbering jumps from 19 to 21; Section 20 and its cross-referenced 20.5 in sec-9.3 are absent). Sections 9.3, 21.3 and 30.5 reference indemnity obligations, indicating a dangling cross-reference to a missing clause — likely flag as missing.

Section 12.4 (second instance) imposes a 24-month, all-territory competition ban on Customer — a direct hit against this rule and inconsistent with sec-12.3, which disclaims any non-compete. Cite the internal conflict when redlining.

Section 12.3 preserves supplier freedom, but Section 7.2 (first instance) requires Customer to disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider — a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal. Assess whether to treat under EXCLUSIVITY or MFN to avoid double-flagging.

Section 7.2 (first instance) obliges Customer to disclose more favourable third-party offers and give Vendor a match right — an MFN running against us, contrary to sec-12.3's disclaimer. Primary home for this rule.

Section 12.4 (first instance) bars Customer from soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months with no general-advertising carve-out — exceeds the narrow, time-limited standard and conflicts with sec-12.3.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and security/service-level termination rights (note the gap at 9.4); no Customer termination for convenience appears, and sec-2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights. Likely missing — confirm against sec-8 and sec-27.3.

Section 8.2 gives 12-month auto-renewals with a 30-day Customer opt-out plus a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension; Section 8.3 caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant — verify against the take-or-pay in sec-2.1.

Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (outside the accepted list), while Section 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts — a direct conflict to resolve in favour of an accepted law and forum.

Section 24.1 permits Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor; 24.4 blocks Vendor remedies on Customer change of control. Section 13.3 confirms licence transferability. Likely compliant.

Section 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data, but Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence to us — a deviation on 'we own what we pay for', in tension with sec-13.2 and sec-14.3.

Sections 13.1–13.3 extend to Affiliates and contractors, grant a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered software, and limit revocation to material uncured breach after cure. Section 14.2's revocable Deliverable licence conflicts — decide whether to raise it here or only under IP to avoid duplicate flags.

Section 22 limits audits to once every 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor-borne cost subject to a 5% underpayment shift, with data-access protections. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer is apparent; sec-2.1's take-or-pay is the nearest penalty-like exposure but belongs under MINCOMMIT. Note also the absence of any service-credit/SLA section in the body (service-level exhibit referenced in sec-2.2).

Section 19 provides professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, term-long for hosted Services), malicious-code and compliance warranties, with re-perform/repair/replace plus refund and termination, expressly non-exclusive for indemnified claims. Likely compliant.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber coverage for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy and non-limitation of liability. Likely compliant.

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per-year, three-year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — a clear deviation and in conflict with sec-12.3's no-minimum-volume disclaimer.

Section 10 addresses access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and refunds, and references a transition period, but check whether any obligation to return/export Customer Data in a usable format or provide transition assistance exists (Section 11, cross-referenced in sec-16.5, is absent from the outline) — may be missing in substance.
